name: Listing 1. A penalty rule stated in the service level agreements for Jade Hotel
contract_text: Jade Hotel will provide a room with a balcony and a view of the sea. If the hotel cannot arrange a sea view room as promised, it shall arrange an alternative room with a luxurious interior design, or a king-size double bed. If this compensation option is unavailable, Jade Hotel will offer two adult members of the tourist family free access to the hotel's spa during their stay. If neither of these compensations could be made, the tourist is entitled to a 50% discount on her accommodation at Jade Hotel upon checkout.

name: Listing 2. Aiken-style pseudocode for a validator that safeguards the creation of per-task transactions
contract_text:
FUNCTION spend_validator (datum?, redeemers, utxo.
transaction)
LET input = inputsAtScriptAddress (transaction, utxo)
LET output = outputsAtScriptAddress (transaction, utxo)
ASSERT Count(input)= 1;
ASSERT hasDatum(input) && isValidDatum(input)
ASSERT transaction is cryptographically signed by all engaging actors specified in the datum
CASE OF redeemer
WHEN Task:
ASSERT Count(output)=1;
ASSERT isValidDatum(output)
ASSERT isValidTransition(input, output)
WHEN Compensated:
ASSERT Count(output) == 0
WHEN Uncompensated:
ASSERT Count(output)==0
ASSERT isLastTask(input)
OTHERWISE:
RETURN False
END CASE
RETURN True
ENDFUNCTION

name: Listing 3. A penalty rule in the car rental business
contract_text: Car renters typically made car rental booking prior to their arrival to allow the car booking company to arrange with associated garages in advance. Upon arrival, the renters expect to be handed in the exact vehicle class they requested in their booking. If the requested model is unfortunately out of reach, the company shall provide an upgraded model within the same segment in a neutral color. Should no upgraded model be readily accessible, the company shall provide a car of a comparable class in a neutral color, as well as waiving all insurance costs from [trusted Insurer] and offer accessories (e.g., child safety seats) for free. If no compliant vehicle is delivered within 120 minutes, the customer is entitled to a compensation package provided by [Trusted Insurer] proportionally scaled based on the customer's tier on the platform.

name: Listing 4. A penalty rule in home decoration services
contract_text: Vietnam is one of a few Asian countries that celebrate the Lunar New Year. Prior to the Tet holiday, Vietnamese families follow the tradition of refreshing and decorating their homes for the new year. DecorX shall complete all Tet's theme installations by the 15th day of Lunar December. Failure to meet this deadline requires X Decor to immediately install a lobby photo zone featuring a 3D backdrop, two 2-meter trees, and integrated lighting. If this option is unavailable, X Decor shall provide a dedicated on-site maintenance attendant to manage and organize the project area daily. If neither is fulfilled, DecorX shall apply a 10% daily reduction of the total contract value until completion at no additional cost, including a free post-Tet dismantling and cleaning service

name: Listing 5. A penalty rule in involuntary denied boarding
contract_text: Skybound Airlines shall ensure the carriage of passengers holding a confirmed reservation on the scheduled flight. In the event of denied boarding against the passenger's will, the Airline shall offer re-routing, under comparable transport conditions, to their final destination at the earliest opportunity. Failing the availability of such re-routing arriving within 4 hours, the Airline shall arrange carriage via an alternative carrier. Should such re routing prove unfeasible, the Airline shall provide the right to care, including hotel accommodation, alongside a full reimbursement of the ticket price and financial compensation equal to 400% of the one-way fare.

name: Listing 6. A penalty rule in the industry of automobile parts
contract_text: XYZ Parts will provide engine components that pass the Automatic Test Process (ATP) defined by Automobiles-X. If a component fails the ATP, XYZ Parts shall deliver an identical replacement within 12 hours. If this replacement is unobtainable, the Contractor will fund equivalent procurement from Vendor B, including all premiums. If procurement via Vendor B cannot be fulfilled, a resident engineer will be deployed within 24 hours to perform on-site sorting and recalibration. If the non-conformity is not remediated within 48 hours of the engineer's arrival, Automobiles-X may apply a payment deduction calculated via a standard formula, factoring in both the item cost and the length of the delay.

name: Listing 7. A penalty rule involving two providers in the domain of tourism
contract_text: During the summer, a tour company offers special sunset boat trips that depart from the easternmost point of the bay area. The trips are held on days with a high likelihood of spotting humpback whales. In case the humpback whales are not spotted during the initial boat trip organized by the tour company, a complimentary second tour will be offered within 3 days; if whales are still not sighted on this follow-up trip, CompanyX will compensate the guest with a full $100 travel voucher redeemable for future excursions, and failure by CompanyX to fulfill this remedy within 14 business days will result in a 50% cash reimbursement of the original ticket price paid to the guest. Soft drinks and snacks are provided on all these tours.

name: Listing 8. A penalty rule involving dual providers for wedding events
contract_text: This is a penalty rule involving three participants: a couple getting married, Vendor-A for furniture & tenting, and Vendor-B for audio-visual & lighting equipment. Prior to the wedding event, if Vendor A fails to install furniture & tenting as agreed upon previously, specifically if the delivery is delayed more than one hour but does not lead to a disrupt of the wedding event, Vendor-A must issue an immediate 25% rental fee credit to the couple within 7 business days. If the delay directly disrupts the event schedule by more than 30 minutes, the compensation escalates to a 50% refund of Vendor-A's total contract value. During the wedding event, if the supplied audio-visual apparatus turn defective or the lighting equipment fails, Vendor-B must provide a functional replacement within 90 minutes. Failure to remedy this on site results in a 80% full refund of the rental cost plus a $300 operational failure fee payable to the couple.

name: Listing 9. Extended penalty involving triple providers for the organization of wedding events
contract_text: This is a penalty rule involving four participants: a couple getting married, Vendor A for furniture & tenting and Vendor-B for audio-visual & lighting equipment, and Vendor-C for catering & food. Prior to the wedding event. if Vendor A fails to install furniture & tenting as agreed upon previously, specifically if the delivery is delayed more than one hour but does not lead to a disrupt of the wedding event, Vendor-A must issue an immediate 25% rental fee credit to the couple within 7 business days. If the delay directly disrupts the event schedule by more than 30 minutes, the compensation escalates to a 50% refund of Vendor-A's total contract value. During the wedding event just before the last hours when the invited guests eat and socialize, if the supplied audo-visual apparatus turn defective or the lighting equipment fails, Vendor-B must provide a functional replacement within 90 minutes. Failure to remedy this on-site results in a 80% full refund of the rental cost plus a $300 operational failure fee payable to the couple. During the last hour of the wedding event, Vendor C must serve all scheduled courses and meals according to the agreed upon event timeline. If the food service fails to arrive or is rendered unconsumable, Vendor C must supply an alternative meal as per the previously specified back-up menu, failing which results in Vendor-C issuing a 100% full refund of the catering contract value plus cover liquidated damages up to $500 for alternative emergency food arrangements within 5 business days.

name: Listing 10. Extended penalty involving triple providers for the organization of shared wedding events
contract_text: This is a penalty rule involving five participants: two couples sharing the same joint wedding service (Couple 1 and Couple 2), Vendor A for furniture and tenting, Vendor-B for audio-visual and lighting equipment, and Vendor C for catering and food. Prior to the wedding event, if Vendor-A fails to install furniture and tenting as agreed upon previously, specifically if the delivery is delayed more than one hour but does not lead to a disruption of the wedding event, Vendor-A must issue an immediate 25% rental fee credit split equally between the two couples within 7 business days if the delay directly disrupts the joint event schedule by more than 30 minutes, the compensation escalates to a 50% refund of Vendor-A's total contract value, divided equally between both couples. During the wedding event just before the last hours when the invited guests eat and socialize, if the supplied audio-visual apparatus turns defective or the lighting equipment fails, Vendor-B must provide a functional replacement within 90 minutes; failure to remedy this on-site results in an 80% full refund of the rental cost plus a $300 operational failure fee payable jointly and divided equally between Couple 1 and Couple 2. During the last hour of the shared wedding event, Vendor C must serve all scheduled courses and meals according to the agreed upon event timeline; if the food service fails to arrive or is rendered unconsumable, Vendor-C must supply an alternative meal as per the previously specified backup menu, failing which results in Vendor-C issuing a 100% full refund of the catering contract value plus covering liquidated damages up to $500 for alternative emergency food arrangements, with all funds distributed equally among both couples within 5 business days.

name: Listing 11. A reciprocal penalty rule tailored for heavy machinery leasing
contract_text: The service level agreement for a heavy machinery leasing service features a reciprocal penalty rule, which outlines specific obligations for both the provider (i.e., lessor/renter out who supplies the crane or excavator) and the client (i.e., lessee/reentee who is a contractor or project owner renting the equipment), avoiding one sided penalty clauses. The client must return the crane or excavator to the designated drop-off point or clear the site for retrieval by the expiration date and time specified in the contract. In case the equipment return is delayed 24 hours without prior written extension, the client shall pay a holdover fee equal to 200% of the standard daily rental rate, plus compensation for any verifiable financial losses incurred by the provider due to subsequent rentals being disrupted. The provider guarantees that the equipment is mechanically sound and fit for purpose. In the event of a mechanical failure not caused by the client, the provider must dispatch a repair unit and restore functionality within 4 hours of notification. Failure to restore the machinery to full working order will result in replacement of the equipment by the provider at their own expense.
